title: Isa's Return
art: The Quran calls Isa, known as Jesus, a sign of the Hour (43:61); that verse is the one shown here.

That Isa will come down at dawn at a white minaret to the east of Damascus, his hands on the wings of two angels, and that drops fall like pearls when he lowers his head, is from the hadith of Sahih Muslim 2937. It is tradition, not Quran, and it is named as such here.
Isa appears only as a distant, steady light far up in the sky, between two columns of light; the angels are never drawn as figures.
The city below is a quiet silhouette of low stone roofs. How the city of that time looked is unknown, so the look of it is imagined, though the buildings are of that age.
Nothing else the hadith describes is shown and nothing is said about it.
imagePrompt: Dawn over a low dark city of stone roofs; above the roofs a single slender white minaret stands in the pale light; far up in the sky a small steady figure of light descends slowly between two tall columns of light, and a few drops of light fall from it like pearls; ink-wash and parchment texture.

beats.say: The Quran calls Isa, known as Jesus, a sign of the Hour. Most commentators read this as his coming down again before the end.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said that he will come down at dawn by a white minaret east of Damascus, his hands on the wings of two angels, and that when he lowers his head, drops fall like pearls.

verse.en: And indeed, Jesus will be [a sign for] knowledge of the Hour, so be not in doubt of it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.
